runs.v: is a multi-ply low-slope membrane that layers a polymer-modified asphalt cap sheet over base plies on the deck. The polymer modifier, styrene-butadiene-styrene or atactic polypropylene, adds flexibility to the redundant, built-up asphalt assembly.

These asphalt-based membranes are enhanced with rubber (SBS) or plastic (APP) polymers, so the polymer-modified asphalt expands and contracts naturally during temperature changes. Supplied in rolled goods and often installed in two or more layers, the overlapping watertight layers create a redundant waterproof barrier, and the material goes down four ways: torch-applied membranes fused tightly to the base layer, hot-mopped asphalt that embeds the plies in hot bitumen, cold-process adhesives that chemically bond the plies without heat, and self-adhered membranes with a factory-applied adhesive backing. Well-suited to low-slope roofing and recommended for flat and low-slope roofs, modified bitumen systems are versatile and adaptable for various roofs.

sections.heading: Disadvantages of Modified Bitumen Roofing, and Modified Bitumen vs. TPO

c.v: The disadvantages of modified bitumen roofing

runs.v: are the open flame of torch application, the heat a dark cap sheet absorbs, and seams and laps that need periodic inspection; of the three common membranes, it is the heaviest and most labor-intensive option to install, TPO and EPDM handle ponding water better, and an aging sheet can micro-crack. Reflective roof options lower cooling costs, so a reflective cap sheet or coating narrows the gap on energy efficiency.

On the other side, modified bitumen roofs are durable and puncture-resistant due to multiple layers: reinforced layers help resist punctures and tears, thick membranes resist tears from foot traffic, and multi-ply systems enhance durability, giving exceptional waterproofing and good weather protection against the elements. Labor-intensive to install yet cost-efficient and affordable over their life, and long-lasting, often for decades, these roofs are resilient against damage and easier to repair than single-ply alternatives, since punctures or local leaks are easy to identify and patch with the same materials set in compatible roof cement, a practical solution for flat roofs with rooftop access. Against TPO, often described as the most specified commercial flat roof membrane in the US, modified bitumen offers multi-ply redundancy, while TPO offers a lighter, reflective single ply, and EPDM, with some roofs reported to last more than 40 years, is the third option. Neither replaces asphalt shingles on a pitched roof, and the right roofing material depends on the roof area, traffic, and budget.

faqs.q: What is the difference between SBS and APP modified bitumen for a West Orange building?

runs.v: SBS-modified bitumen, modified with styrene-butadiene-styrene rubber, provides exceptional elasticity and cold-weather flexibility and resists freeze-thaw cycles better than APP-modified bitumen, modified with atactic polypropylene, which offers superior direct resistance to ultraviolet radiation and heat but runs stiffer in cold. Newark Quality Roofing installs SBS modified bitumen for the freeze-thaw cycling West Orange shares with the Essex County climate, per ARMA modified-bitumen guidance.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial modified bitumen roof in West Orange?

runs.v: A commercial, multi-family, or attached modified bitumen roof requires a permit once the work exceeds 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, while a detached one- or two-family flat-roof section counts as ordinary maintenance and requires no permit.
